newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy unions to meet on metalworkers, mull strike.
newsitem.headline: Italy unions to meet on metalworkers, mull strike.

text.p: Italian union leaders were due to meet at 1600 GMT on Tuesday to discuss a bitter months-long pay dispute in the engineering and metalworking sectors and could decide to call a general strike, trades union sources said.
Engineering and metalworkers have already held several hours of strikes over renewal of their contracts for the 1996-98 contract period. Their last contracts expired in June.
The sources said Tuesday's meeting would bring together the leaders of Italy's three main labour confederations, CGIL, CISL and UIL and their sectoral unions, FIOM, FIM and UILM.

Leaders of Federmeccanica, the sector's employers' association, were meeting in Milan to discuss a government proposal that workers should be given a 200,000 lire ($130) a month pay rise for the period.
The proposal has been welcomed by unions, which sought 230,000 lire a month for their 1.7 million members in a sector that accounts for some 40 percent of Italian manufacturing output.
Federmeccanica has rejected the proposal and offered to raise pay by no more than 139,000 lire a month.
Labour Minister Tiziano Treu was due to begin separate talks with employers and unions on Wednesday.
CISL leader Sergio D'Antoni warned on Saturday of "inevitable social conflict" if employers did not soften their position.
